- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are trending up, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% if recent price momentum is strong.
- If model shows a sharp spike in forecast followed by a drop, it often overcorrects; cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome exceeds model by >5% in 3+ consecutive days, apply mean reversion bias: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for next period if sentiment is trending upward.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model often underreacts; increase forecast sensitivity by 10–20% for volatile periods.
